title: Position effect at the SOX3 locus by an interchromosomal insertion causes hereditary spastic paraplegia.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: no PMCID, no open full text, no supplement listing, no accessions in text or text-mined, no NCBI GEO/SRA/BioProject links (only two PMC links, likely citing articles), no Zenodo/Dryad hits on the DOI.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything else comes from the abstract: one Danish family, a 149-kb insertion from 4q24 into Xq27.1, iPSCs (induced pluripotent stem cells) from affected individuals, Hi-C (genome-wide chromatin contact mapping) and RNA-seq in derived neurons, CRISPR perturbations.

a1_downloadable.note: No deposited dataset found by any route; patient-derived sequencing is likely controlled access or unreleased. Checked metadata only.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No label table exists; this is a mechanistic study of one structural variant, so any target (e.g. 'pathogenic position effect') would have to be constructed.

a5_enough_rows.note: One family and one variant; a handful of iPSC lines and Hi-C/RNA-seq samples at most, from the abstract alone.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Processed Hi-C/RNA-seq for a few samples would fit, but nothing is available.

honest_claim_h3: No model claim is possible: the paper characterises one structural variant in one family and no data is deposited.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA content of an inserted segment to predict whether it rewires nearby gene regulation and changes gene expression.
plain_idea.train_on: Structural variants with their 3D genome-contact and expression effects; this paper offers one example (unknown sample count, nothing deposited).
plain_idea.predict: Change in expression of the nearby gene (here SOX3), measured by RNA-seq in neurons derived from patient stem cells.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Clinical geneticists could flag non-coding structural variants likely to cause disease, but one variant cannot train or test such a model.

ml_idea: None viable: a single-family mechanistic case study could at most act as one anecdotal test case for 3D-genome predictors such as Akita or C.Origami, not as training data.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Search GEO for the paper's Hi-C/RNA-seq deposit; even if it exists, n is one variant.

verdict_reason: Single-family case study of one structural variant; no deposited data found, no label table, and n is far too small (A1, A2, A5 fail).
